## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vaṭṭakajātaka* (Ja 394), titled "The Quail", is a birth story situated in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework preserved in its commentary, the Buddha recounted this story while dwelling at Jetavana in reference to a greedy monk (*lolo bhikkhu*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. Addressing the monk, the Buddha revealed that this was not the first time he had displayed unrestrained greed: in a past existence in Benares, he had fed on carcasses of elephants, oxen, horses, and humans, but still remained dissatisfied and ventured into the forest in search of richer food [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883].
In the story of the past, the greedy monk was born as a crow and the Bodhisatta was born as a quail [Fausböll 1883]. Seeing the quail healthy and plump while he himself was emaciated, the crow questioned how the quail thrived on rough, dry grass-seeds with little nourishment, whereas the crow remained lean despite feeding on meat [Fausböll 1883]. The verses explain that living wickedly among enemies in constant anxiety prevents the crow from gaining strength, whereas a contented life in peace brings well-being [Fausböll 1883]. At the conclusion of the teaching, the greedy monk attained stream-entry (*sotāpatti*) [Fausböll 1883].
SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the text across four languages, listing no curated parallels in other Buddhist canonical traditions [SuttaCentral]. Machine analysis by DharmaNexus identifies eight internal Pali text-reuse segments shared between the verses and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (amounting to 971 characters, spanning §1.4–4.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects five minor alignments with the Tibetan *Mahāvyutpatti* (D4346), though these represent lexical matches rather than thematic parallels [DharmaNexus].
